name: Benin
tagline: Where vodun comes from, and the palaces of Dahomey
summary: Ouidah is the source of vodun and a departure point of the Atlantic slave trade, Abomey holds the earthen palaces of the kings of Dahomey, and Ganvie is a town of thirty thousand people on stilts in a lagoon.
when: November to February, the main dry season. The Vodun festival is on 10 January.

entries.caption: Ganvie
entries.description: Thirty thousand people living on stilts in Lake Nokoue, moving between houses by pirogue.
entries.subject: stilt houses and pirogues in the lake village of Ganvie

entries.caption: Pendjari and the Atakora
entries.description: The Atakora hills in the northwest, and the Pendjari river running along the park.
entries.subject: the Pendjari river running below wooded hills in the Atakora

entries.caption: Pendjari
entries.description: Lion, elephant, buffalo and cheetah in one of the last strongholds of the West African lion.
entries.subject: a West African lion in tall grass in Pendjari National Park

entries.caption: The W-Arly-Pendjari Complex
entries.description: The largest intact ecosystem in West Africa, run across three countries.
entries.subject: elephants at a waterhole in Pendjari at the end of the dry season

entries.caption: The Atakora Range
entries.description: Six hundred metres of quartzite ridge in the northwest, with the Somba country under it.
entries.subject: the quartzite ridges of the Atakora range in northern Benin

entries.caption: Tanougou
entries.description: Falls off the Atakora into a deep pool, swimmable and cold.
entries.subject: the Tanougou waterfall falling into a green pool

entries.caption: Lake Nokoue and the Oueme
entries.description: The lagoon behind Cotonou, and the Oueme running down to it through the delta.
entries.subject: fishing nets and stakes across Lake Nokoue at dawn

entries.caption: A Hundred Kilometres of Atlantic
entries.description: Grand-Popo and Ouidah, with heavy surf and coconut palms right down to the sand.
entries.subject: palms and heavy Atlantic surf on the beach at Grand-Popo

entries.caption: The Sacred Forests
entries.description: Kpasse at Ouidah and the groves around it, protected because they are vodun sites.
entries.subject: tall trees and a shrine in the sacred forest of Kpasse at Ouidah

entries.caption: Pirogue and Pendjari
entries.description: Poling through Ganvie in the morning, and a game drive in the north two days later.
entries.subject: a pirogue being poled between stilt houses at Ganvie

entries.caption: Where Vodun Comes From
entries.description: Not a folk survival — a living religion with millions of followers, and a public holiday.
entries.subject: a vodun ceremony with drumming and white-clad participants

entries.caption: Fon, Yoruba, Bariba, Somba
entries.description: The Fon of Dahomey in the south, the Somba in the Atakora with their fortified houses.
entries.subject: a Somba tata fortified mud house in the Atakora

entries.caption: Amiwo and Grilled Fish
entries.description: Amiwo — maize with tomato and chicken — and fish straight off the Grand-Popo beach.
entries.subject: a plate of amiwo with grilled chicken and pepper sauce

entries.caption: The Vodun Festival
entries.description: 10 January at Ouidah, on the beach, and it is a religious event before it is a spectacle.
entries.subject: crowds and dancers on the beach at the Ouidah vodun festival

entries.caption: Applique and Bronze
entries.description: The Abomey applique banners that recorded the kings' reigns, and Fon bronze casting.
entries.subject: an Abomey applique cloth banner with royal symbols

entries.caption: The Royal Palaces of Abomey
entries.description: Twelve palaces of the kings of Dahomey, in earth, with bas-reliefs telling the history.
entries.subject: earthen bas-reliefs on a wall of the royal palaces of Abomey

entries.caption: The Route of the Slaves
entries.description: Four kilometres from Ouidah's auction square to the Door of No Return on the beach.
entries.subject: the Door of No Return arch on the beach at Ouidah

entries.caption: Cotonou, Porto-Novo, Abomey
entries.description: A port that never stops, a colonial capital, and the seat of a kingdom.
entries.subject: the Dantokpa market and motorcycle taxis in Cotonou

entries.caption: Earth and Afro-Brazilian
entries.description: Somba tata towers in the north, and Afro-Brazilian merchant houses in Ouidah and Porto-Novo.
entries.subject: an Afro-Brazilian merchant house with shuttered windows in Porto-Novo

entries.caption: Zemidjan
entries.description: The motorcycle taxis are the transport system, and their yellow shirts are the uniform.
entries.subject: yellow-shirted zemidjan motorcycle taxi riders waiting at a junction

entries.caption: Ganvie by Pirogue
entries.description: A whole town on water, reached by boat, which no child has ever found boring.
entries.subject: children in a pirogue among the stilt houses of Ganvie

entries.caption: Walking the Atakora
entries.description: Somba villages, quartzite ridges and the Tanougou pool, on foot from Natitingou.
entries.subject: a footpath through Atakora hills past a Somba compound

entries.caption: A Few Good Ones
entries.description: Lodges at Pendjari and on the coast at Grand-Popo, and good hotels in Cotonou.
entries.subject: a beach lodge terrace among palms at Grand-Popo

entries.caption: Pendjari, Community-Run
entries.description: Managed since 2017 by African Parks with the villages around it, and the lion count is up.
entries.subject: a ranger scanning grassland from a vehicle in Pendjari

entries.caption: Stilts and Reflection
entries.description: Ganvie at first light, when the water is still and the houses double.
entries.subject: stilt houses reflected in still water at dawn in Ganvie

entries.caption: Possotome and Lake Aheme
entries.description: A quiet lake west of Ouidah with fishing villages and hot springs on its shore.
entries.subject: fishing boats on the shore of Lake Aheme at Possotome

entries.caption: Why Benin
entries.description: Vodun at its source, the palaces of Dahomey, and West Africa's best-run national park.
entries.subject: a vodun devotee in white before a shrine at Ouidah
